verdict.line: You lose the trades from level 1 to 5 if you stand in his Q chain and let his E heal him back up, but you win the lane from level 9 onward once Thornmail and Sunfire Aegis gut his sustain.

brief.thesis: Aatrox's entire kit is built to win short trades and heal through them: Q (The Darkin Blade) resets down to a 6s cooldown at rank 5 for repeated poke, Deathbringer Stance periodically empowers an auto with bonus magic damage and a heal, and E (Umbral Dash) heals him passively whenever he lands damage while also letting him disengage. Ornn has no sustain tool to match that and no real threat until R (Call of the Forge God) comes online at 6, so the matchup is a 50.3% coinflip over 1556 games that is actually two different matchups: a losing poke war pre-6, and a winning tank-vs-bruiser stall once Grievous Wounds items (Bramble Vest, Thornmail) shut off all three of his heals.

theirWindow.when: Deathbringer Stance lit and E off cooldown
theirWindow.what: He has a free empowered auto plus a dash to land it and sustain off the damage. Don't trade face-to-face here — let him walk the poke and reset to CS instead of matching autos.

yourWindow.when: Right after he uses E (Umbral Dash)
yourWindow.what: Umbral Dash is on a 9-5s cooldown and is both his stick and his escape — without it he can't heal off you or leave. Punish with Q (Volcanic Rupture) for the slow or dash your own E (Searing Charge) into him toward terrain for the knockup.

start.why: The flat damage reduction on autos directly blunts his auto-reliant poke pattern and the Deathbringer Stance procs you can't avoid.

boots.why: Reduces the physical damage from both his normal autos and his empowered Deathbringer Stance auto, which is where most of his early lane damage comes from.

core.why: Early Grievous Wounds on hit starts cutting his Deathbringer Stance and Umbral Dash healing before he snowballs the lane.
Adds HP and armor plus passive burn damage so you stop losing the farming war while you're behind on trades.
Full Grievous Wounds on hit against a champion whose kit heals from three separate sources (passive, E, R) is the single biggest swing in this matchup.
Stacking resistances let you actually win extended fights once his early-game damage lead is neutralized.

situational.when: he or his team is leaning on healing/lifesteal and you need the Grievous Wounds without giving up magic resist
their damage shifts heavily magic and you need the spell shield instead of more armor

runes.keystoneWhy: Sustained HP damage and healing on every proc keeps you in lane through his auto-heavy poke instead of losing the war of attrition before your items come online.

summoners.why: This is the dominant page at 73.9% pick and 49.5% win rate — Teleport lets you reset off bad early trades and still make it back to scale into your level 9+ power spike instead of being forced to fight before you're ready.

playing.title: Don't trade into empowered autos
playing.detail: When Deathbringer Stance is up, he gets bonus magic damage and a heal on his next auto — disengage and farm instead of matching hits.

playing.title: Dash out of Infernal Chains before the drag
playing.detail: His W deals damage on the first hit, but if you don't leave the impact area quickly you get pulled to the center and hit again. Use E (Searing Charge) immediately to get clear and avoid the second instance.

playing.title: Punish his E cooldown, not his Q
playing.detail: Umbral Dash is both his stick and his heal; it's on a short 9-5s cooldown but still a real window. Walk up with Q (Volcanic Rupture) poke only when E is down.

playing.title: Farm through levels 1-5
playing.detail: You lose the solo-kill race at this stage per the measured data — prioritize CS and avoid extended trades until your tank items land.

playing.title: All-in once Bramble Vest and Thornmail are both up
playing.detail: Grievous Wounds removes his Deathbringer Stance heal, his Umbral Dash heal, and his R World Ender sustain boost at the same time — this is your real power spike, not level 6.

playing.title: Use R to flip a losing trade
playing.detail: Call of the Forge God's elemental slows and applies Brittle on first contact; recast by charging into it to redirect a knockup onto him for a follow-up all-in.

playing.title: Respect his three-hit Q chain
playing.detail: The Darkin Blade swings up to three times with a different area each swing — back off after the first hit instead of eating the full chain.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate/sample-size figures above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the matchup read — why the trades go this way and when the power shifts — is my own analysis of the ability mechanics, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Move away from Aatrox’s (Q), while using [E] and [W] to block his (W). Try to focus on farming lane and growing instead of fighting him often as he can recover a lot of health.
